entry_text: Aligned the NO.2 panel after the bracket was found slack, checked the beam on a shore mark.
Bled the fuel system after the filter change.
Brake band relined on the main haul winch and the test load run.
Casualty bag inspected, contents correct.
Changed oil and filters on no 2.
Charger float voltage set wrong, was cooking the bank. Reset and logged the readings.
Checked the AIS position against the chart.
Cleaned terminals and greased. No damage.
Cleared a blockage in the suction strainer.
Compressor run up and the receiver drained.
Contractor could not find it. Found it in 1.5 hrs on the drawings, a wrong terminal from 1981.
Descended to the mid-course for a look.
Discrimination not right between the incomer and no 2 way, adjusted settings and proved.
Dressed a cut hand for 3rd.
Empties sent back with the boat.
Filter changed on the power pack.
Governor hunting under load, adjusted droop and stability until it settled.
Greased the derrick head and the slew ring.
Greased the winch and checked the pawl.
Gutters cleared of weed and grit.
Handled a live DSC distress alert, acknowledged, took the traffic on ch.16 and passed it on.
Helipad swept and the nets checked.
Lamp changer stepping twice, dismantled the ratchet and dressed the pawl faces.
Landing in the dark by torch, worked the swell and put everyone up dry.
Load-tested the standby bank, No.2 cell down to 232 V, taken out and shorted round.
Load-tested the standby bank, no.2 cell down to 3.6 bar, taken out and shorted round.
Load-tested the standby bank, no.3 cell down to 2.4 ohm, taken out and shorted round.
Load-tested the standby bank, no.3 cell down to 48 psi, taken out and shorted round.
Logged the search traffic.
Made up a new hose to length with the on-station swager, pressure tested before fitting.
Managed a suspected heart case overnight, radio medical advice taken hourly.
Nothing heard on the distress frequency.
Painted the lantern roof.
Pointing made good on the south wall.
Pressure reading 11.2 V, about normal.
Pressure reading 2.4 ohm, about normal.
Produced the dilapidation schedule for the district ahead of the automation survey.
Quarterly inspection carried out, report filed.
Ran the boat off the rock in NW 7 gusting 9, held her off the steps while the stores went across.
Ran the boat off the rock in W 8, held her off the steps while the stores went across.
Re-terminated the no.1 outgoing at the board, IR tested at 0.8 ohm before re-energising.
Re-terminated the No.1 outgoing at the board, IR tested at 232 V before re-energising.
Re-terminated the No.1 outgoing at the board, IR tested at 3.6 bar before re-energising.
Recovered a broken-down punt under tow in a rising sea, made fast and got her in.
Reorganised the store below and set a minimum stock for the consumables.
Reorganised the watch bill so the new men were always paired with an experienced hand.
Rewired the changeover contactor arrangement, tested on both feeds and left in auto.
Rigged a rebelay past the corbel and worked the whole face in two drops.
Set up the auto-start sequence on no 2 after the card was changed, timings adjusted.
Set up the haul for a heavy lift in a poor sea, rigged a preventer on the fall.
Showed SAK the lamp changer routine.
Started No.1 set and ran on load 6 hrs.
Stood by at the landing for the boat.
Stood by for evacuation, stood down.
Survival drill with the station party.
Synchronised no.1 onto the board manually, the auto sync had drifted off.
Talked the pilot in on the radio when the pad lights failed, torches on the corners.
Took the supernumerary round the plant.
Topped the hydraulic reservoir, 2 gal.
Topped up cells, 2 gal distilled water used.
Treated PK for a crush injury to the hand, splinted and kept him until the boat came.
Winch brake adjusted a little.
Wire brushed and primed the door frame.
Worked the mast head in E 6, two-point attachment throughout.
Worked the mast head in NE 5, two-point attachment throughout.
Worked the mast head in NW 7 gusting 9, two-point attachment throughout.
Worked the mast head in S 4, two-point attachment throughout.
Worked the mast head in SW 6, two-point attachment throughout.
Worked the mast head in W 8, two-point attachment throughout.
Wrote the safe system for the lantern work and had it countersigned by the district.
